newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says German bank will grant $90 mln oil loan.
newsitem.headline: Iran says German bank will grant $90 mln oil loan.

text.p: Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank (West LB) will grant Iran a $90 million loan to develop its Soroush oilfield, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.

IRNA, quoting an article in Saturday's daily Iran newspaper, said West LB would give the loan to the Iranian Offshore Engineering Construction Co (IOEC) to expand and renovate the offshore field. IOEC won the development contract on the Soroush field earlier this year.
The information was attributed to the production manager of offshore regions of the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC). He was not named.
IRNA also said: "A petroleum expert told Iran (newspaper) that according to the contract signed between the Iranian and German sides, the repayment of the loan will be through the sale of crude oil."
Independent confirmation of the deal was not immediately available.

On Thursday, a powerful U.S. senator warned West LB against making the loan. In a letter to West LB chief executive Friedel Neuber, New York Republican Alfonse D'Amato said the deal would be a clear violation of the 1996 Iran Libya Sanctions Act.
D'Amato was a key author of the legislation, which imposes U.S. sanctions on any company that invests $40 million or more in a 12-month period in the energy sectors of Iran or Libya.
He said that if West LB went ahead with the loan, it would become a "pariah company known for supporting rogue states".
West LB is Germany's largest publicly-owned regional bank, or Landesbank.
